title: Adverbs
subtitle: How, when, where and how often.
objectives: Identify an adverb and what it modifies
Name the main kinds of adverb
Place an adverb where it does not confuse the sentence

cards.title: An adverb answers a question about the verb
cards.text: Adjectives describe things. Adverbs describe actions. How, when, where, and how often.

cards.title: Four questions, four kinds
cards.text: Ask the question and the kind names itself.

cards.title: Most come from an adjective plus -ly
cards.text: With a few spelling rules and a few that refuse entirely.
points: **fast, hard, late** do not change at all.

cards.title: Which question does it answer?
cards.text: Five kinds, five questions. If none fits, it is not an adverb.

question.text: Which word is the adverb? 'He wrapped his hands carefully.'
question.explain: It tells you how he wrapped them, which is an adverb of manner.

cards.title: A coach speaks almost entirely in adverbs
cards.text: The verb is obvious. What the coach is correcting is how it is done.
points: **You already know the verb.** The adverb is the instruction.

question.text: Turn 'easy' into an adverb. One word.
question.explain: Ends in -y, so it becomes -ily: easily.

cards.title: Put it where it cannot be misread
cards.text: Some adverbs change meaning entirely depending on where they sit.
points: **Only I fixed the fan.** Nobody else did.
**I only fixed the fan.** I did nothing else to it.
**I fixed only the fan.** Not the lamp.

cards.title: Adverbs are how a game describes its own feel
cards.text: Patch notes and item text lean on them constantly.
points: **Move the adverb** and the patch note means something else.

question.text: Which sentence means 'I did nothing to it except fix it'?
options: I fixed the fan only yesterday.
question.explain: Placed before the verb, 'only' limits the action.

cards.title: How is it moving?
cards.alt: A cartoon snail in a racing helmet inching along a racetrack lane with comic motion lines
cards.text: Slowly. That is an adverb of manner, and it is the question it answers.

cards.title: Literature Review: Don Quixote, Chapter 19: The Strolling Players
cards.text: A cart of actors in costume crosses the road, and Quixote reads them as demons.
points: **He never looks closely.** Frequency and manner.
**The adverbs carry the pace** of the whole scene.

terms.def: A word describing a verb, an adjective or another adverb.
To add information to another word.

cards.title: What to remember
points: Adverbs answer how, when, where and how often.
Most are an adjective plus -ly; good becomes well.
fast, hard and late are already adverbs.
Placement matters: 'only' moves and the meaning moves with it.

quiz.explain: It can also describe an adjective or another adverb, but the verb is the main job.
quiz.objective: Identify an adverb and what it modifies

quiz.text: 'He trained hard yesterday.' Which is an adverb of time?
quiz.objective: Name the main kinds of adverb

quiz.text: Turn 'careful' into an adverb. One word.
Turn 'easy' into an adverb. One word.

quiz.objective: Name the main kinds of adverb

quiz.text: Which sentence means nobody else fixed it?
quiz.objective: Place an adverb where it does not confuse the sentence

quiz.explain: Fast, hard and late are already adverbs. 'Fastly' is not a word.

quiz.text: In 'she reloads automatically', the adverb tells you…
quiz.objective: Identify an adverb and what it modifies

quiz.text: Which is an adverb of place?
quiz.objective: Name the main kinds of adverb

quiz.text: Moving an adverb never changes a sentence's meaning.
quiz.explain: 'Only' is the clearest counter-example: three positions, three meanings.
quiz.objective: Place an adverb where it does not confuse the sentence

quiz.text: In Chapter 19, what does Quixote think the actors are?
quiz.explain: A cart of costumed players, and he charges them immediately.
quiz.objective: Identify an adverb and what it modifies

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 9 English. Adverbs are organised by the question they answer, which makes the four kinds self-naming and removes most of the memorisation. The -ly formation is given with its two spelling rules and its exceptions, and 'fastly' is addressed directly because it is a predictable over-generalisation of exactly the kind seen in weeks 2 and 7. The placement section built on 'only' is the most useful part of the lesson: four words, three positions, three different meanings, which makes word order feel consequential rather than cosmetic.
discussion: What four questions do adverbs answer?
How many meanings can you get from moving 'only'?
extension: Write a coaching instruction using an adverb of manner and one of frequency.
Move 'only' through a sentence and write out each meaning.
misconceptions: Adding -ly to words that are already adverbs.
